key_insight: PEA spacers improve crystal morphology and suppress lattice defects, making PEA2PbI4 more resistant to ambient light and thermal degradation than BA2PbI4.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection is a useful stability lever for two-dimensional perovskite devices, alongside structural engineering, surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Evaluated ambient photo- and thermal stability using confocal micro-Raman spectroscopy.
Probed chemical degradation using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, but PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite sharing organic-loss and PbI2/Pb0 decomposition pathways with BA-based crystals.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or device-efficiency measurements, so improved material stability should not be equated with demonstrated solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
